text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.74% today to $137.20, continuing a sharp five-day rally that's added 5.3% since late August. The driver is clear: escalating military conflict in the Middle East between Iran and the U.S., along with Iranian strikes on U.S. Gulf allies, has pushed oil prices higher. Brent crude climbed above $95 per barrel and U.S. crude is now at $91.48, up from the lows of late August. For an oil producer like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices directly improve profitability on the barrels they pump and sell.

This move fits a broader pattern where geopolitical risk in the Persian Gulf — the world's most critical oil chokepoint — translates immediately into stock gains for large energy companies. With over 17 million barrels of oil transiting the Strait of Hormuz daily, any threat to that supply route tightens markets and lifts prices across the board.
